## Original user question (solution sections removed)
Title: How to compose a larger circuit onto a smaller circuit in Qiskit, adding extra quantum registers to some fixed list

$\newcommand{\ket}[1]{|{#1}\rangle}$ I have a Qiskit quantum circuit for multiplication $M$, that I want to onto another qiskit quantum circuit for inner product of vectors $I$. $M$ uses some ancillary qubits to perform the map $\ket{a}\ket{b}\ket{c} \mapsto \ket{a}\ket{b}\ket{c\oplus (a\cdot b)}$. Ideally when I compose $M$ onto $I$ as a subroutine, I would only want to declare and map the quantum states (registers) of $I$ that I care about: $\ket{a},\ket{b},\ket{c}$ and let the additional qubits be counted as some ancillas in $I$, maybe in some fixed register , whose length can be appropriately extended. According to the Qiskit documentation, to , $M$ can be narrower or of equal width to $I$, and methods like have been deprecated and removed. How can I go about doing this, if at all? I would be okay using any other SDK like Cirq, as I need a QASM2 at the end. But my circuits use classically controlled operations, which Cirq does not seem to support.

```
compose
```

```
anc
```

```
compose
```

```
extend
```

```
dump
```
